basis: Deafness, short terminal phalanges and intellectual disability are defining manifestations, each reported in 30-79%.
Chronic venous dysfunction defines the disease; qualifying skin damage across the broad concept is not established at >=30%.
Congenital peripheral axonal neuropathy and encephalopathy; respiratory and swallowing dysfunction reflect neural weakness, not intrinsic lung or gut damage.
Combined immunodeficiency with T-cell lymphopenia in 5/5 patients and B/NK-cell depletion in 3/5.
Defined by neurodevelopmental impairment, intellectual disability, epilepsy and sometimes structural brain anomalies.
Heterozygous beta-globin deficiency causes microcytosis with absent or mild anemia; severe thalassemia complications do not apply.
Progressive cerebral white-matter degeneration; blindness is 5-29%, and ovarian insufficiency lacks a qualifying frequency for this subtype.
Encephalocele and anencephaly identify congenital structural defects of the central nervous system; additional organ involvement is unspecified.
Molecular subtype of mature B-cell lymphoma; no particular extranodal organ is established as commonly damaged.
Joint/connective-tissue abnormalities and skin fragility or hyperextensibility span the group; severe valve disease belongs to a specific subtype.
Severe developmental delay in 7/7 with epilepsy and brain malformations; isolated cardiac and ocular reports do not establish >=30% across the cohort.
Congenital absence or hypoplasia of the fibula with associated limb and joint deformities; extra-skeletal abnormalities are very rare.
Corneal dystrophy causes recurrent erosions, opacities and progressive visual impairment.
Inherited high myopia, reported in 12/12 patients; associated retinal complications remain within the ocular axis.
Progressive degeneration of choroid, retinal pigment epithelium and retina; ocular vascular findings do not establish systemic vascular disease.
Congenital bifid nose; the nasal structures fall within the pulmonary axis.
Primary malignant bone tumor producing predominantly osteoid matrix.
Inherited mitochondrial complex I deficiency presenting as optic neuropathy; optic atrophy and progressive visual loss occur in 3/3.
Neoplasm arising in the vagina, a reproductive organ outside the specified axes.
EBV-associated neoplastic disease; anatomical sites and blood-cell origin vary across lymphoid, epithelial and mesenchymal subtypes.
Severe valve/aortic disease, skeletal defects and emphysema (100%) define this form; ectopia lentis 80-99%. Cutis laxa 80-99% omitted under the four-axis cap.
Thiamine deficiency causes encephalopathy and amnestic brain injury; abnormal eye movements are neurologic, and common direct cardiac damage is not established.
Multiple benign lipomas occupy subcutaneous tissue; thrombocytopenia and purpura are very rare.
Isolated congenital gonadotropin deficiency impairs gonadal hormone production; no broader neurologic syndrome is specified.
Functional ovarian corpus luteum cyst is a reproductive disorder; endocrine dysfunction is not established by the cyst itself.
